scope: Blocked source-only revision of ControllerHandler queue-byte-budget design; no Rust patch
decision: Do not adopt until wake, receiver lifecycle, unwind, poison, reentrancy and native concurrency controls are independently reviewed and qualified.
review_findings: A sole reserved permit can make shutdown Stop fail Full, then rejection can return the permit without waking the actor.
A reserved permit may send after receiver closure; a direct response future may then hang while the sender remains alive.
Both Busy and InvalidConfig map to transport HandlerError and connection closure; repeated small admissions can starve a large one.
revision: A synchronous gate sketch fences all producers, stop signaling, actor post-receive stop checks and receiver lifetime; potentially reentrant drops and replies happen outside. The protocol remains conditional, unimplemented, and blocked.
validation: Verified source and peer hashes plus bounded source observations with verify-source.py.
Reproduced the bounded idealized state model output: Q=1 and Q=2, valid/invalid producer, empty/seeded queue, normal actor work or modeled actor failure.
A peer examined the draft sketch and reproduced the model output; a bound independent receipt is pending.
limitations: No Cargo, compiler, Rust/native test, actual Tokio execution, actor/WAL/network test or benchmark.
The toy model excludes multiple producers, bytes, actual allocation, wake failure, panic/poison within send or gate, reentrant destructors, memory ordering and scheduler fairness.
All old successful behavior cannot be preserved under the desired byte bound without changing allocation/reuse semantics. The planned errors and transport connection impact are observable.
The Q*L estimate covers queued input Vec capacities only; active work, replies, callers, allocation overhead, buffers and RSS are outside.
No production-readiness, fastest-performance or release-readiness claim.
